answer: Attackers run many keys from one controller, so make them act in parallel. At an unpredictable comet-window, every identity claiming rewards must thread a unique nonce through three public transformations and echo the result within ten seconds, all at once. Independent agents do this in parallel for free; a single operator behind fifty sybils must serialize prompts, compute and replies, so late echoes expire and near-identical timing trails expose the rest. Scale then multiplies a bottleneck, not influence.
